headline: Sensex ends 333 points higher, Nifty crosses 23,200 snapping 2-day fall
why: Markets snapped a two-day losing streak aided by positive global cues.
Rally in stocks holding exposure to the newly opened NSE IPO.
Strong buying momentum in specific midcap stocks following major deal wins.
whatHappening: Sensex gained 333 points, closing with Nifty above 23,200.
Rupee weakened below the 96 per dollar mark in early trade.
NSE's Rs 22,569 crore IPO opened, boosting stocks like IFCI and New India Assurance.
Glass Wall Systems stock surged 32% within two days of listing.

stocksInNews.sources: Surged 11% after securing a 15-year Punjab PET-CT deal
Rallied up to 9% following the opening of the NSE IPO
Gained due to stock exposure as the NSE IPO opened
Remained in focus during morning trade

summary: Indian benchmark indices snapped a two-day decline as the Sensex added 333 points to close above 23,200. Action was driven by the Rs 22,569 crore NSE IPO opening and positive stock-specific order wins.
